topic: The Morning Search Trap: Why starting your day with Google Maps is a productivity mistake.

hooks.text: Do you open Google Maps first thing every morning?
Are you losing billable hours scrolling Google Maps each sunrise?
Myth: Early map searches boost leads. Fact: They drain your earnings.

posts.linkedin:
Freelancers waste morning hours manually searching for local leads instead of doing billable work.

A typical start of the day begins with good intentions, but within a few minutes you are zooming into Google Maps, opening a dental clinic, a gym, or an accounting firm, copying phone numbers, and pasting them into a blank document. By lunch you have spent your freshest energy on repetitive data entry rather than writing proposals or delivering work for existing clients.

What I provide is a simple Excel sheet that lists pre‑qualified local businesses pulled from Google Places. Each row contains verified contact details, the number of online reviews, a basic check of whether the business has a website, and an indication if the location has opened recently. The sheet is ready for anyone who sells services such as marketing, video editing, design, SEO, bookkeeping, or consulting to local owners.

The process is straightforward. First you tell me the type of businesses you want to target and the service you offer. I then extract the relevant listings from Google Places, run a quick website presence check, and arrange all the information into clear columns. Once the sheet is prepared, you review it to confirm that the entries meet your criteria before using the data for outreach.

Having the list already organized lets you keep your daily momentum. Sourcing contacts and reaching out require different mindsets; when the spreadsheet sits on your desk you can move directly into personalized outreach during your most productive morning hours, leaving the rest of the day free for client delivery and project work.

An honest limitation is that the spreadsheet does not write the emails or make the phone calls for you. It only organizes market information; building trust with a business owner still depends on your own pitch and the quality of the service you provide.

I am happy to discuss whether this approach fits your outreach routine. You pay only after you approve the work. DM me with the word LEADS if you want to discuss.
posts.bluesky: Scrolling Maps for leads eats your best morning hours. Getting a clean Excel sheet with local business contacts, reviews, and website status lets you pitch straight away. DM LEADS to learn more.

replies.if_they_say: How much does the lead sheet cost?
replies.reply: Hi! Thanks for reaching out. I keep pricing simple and tailored to what you need, but first: what service do you sell and which local business categories are you planning to reach out to? Prefer a quick chat here or over WhatsApp?

replies.if_they_say: Does this work for video editors and social media agencies?
replies.reply: Yes, absolutely. The sheet covers local businesses with contact info, review counts, and website presence, which makes it easy to spot who needs content or marketing help. Quick question: are you targeting specific cities or specific business types like clinics and gyms?

replies.if_they_say: How do I know the contact details are actually verified?
replies.reply: The data is sourced directly via Google Places along with website checks, including active phone numbers and review status. You can review the sheet first, and as with all my work, you pay only after you approve it. What kind of clients are you looking for right now?
